title: Boost Converter (step-up)
summary: Non-isolated step-up converter; in continuous conduction the output voltage equals the input divided by (1 - D).

ports.name: in
ports.description: Positive input supply rail feeding the inductor.

ports.name: sw
ports.description: Switching node between the inductor, the low-side switch, and the rectifier.

ports.name: out
ports.description: Regulated step-up output rail across the filter capacitor and load.

ports.name: pwm
ports.description: Gate-drive command for the low-side switch from the controller.

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Steady-state duty cycle of the low-side switch.

design_equations.name: inductor_current
design_equations.description: Average inductor current equals the input current.

design_equations.name: output_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple for an ideal capacitor (capacitor supplies the load during the on-time).

design_equations.name: rhp_zero
design_equations.description: Right-half-plane zero frequency that limits the achievable loop bandwidth.

control_notes: The boost control-to-output transfer function contains a right-half-plane (RHP) zero whose frequency drops with load and duty cycle. Voltage-mode loop bandwidth must stay well below f_rhpz (typically below a third of it), which forces a slow loop. Current-mode control is preferred because it removes the inductor pole from the voltage loop, though the RHP zero remains.

reference.source: J. Marcos Alonso, Modelling, Control and Simulation of DC-DC Converters
